persona: Buyer for an online t-shirt shop

designs.title: How Beer Is Made
designs.why: Clear, giftable 'beer nerd' concept that reads instantly as a flow chart from distance; clean bold line work and crisp sans type hold up at full size and white-on-black is the strongest of the three on a product page. Downsides: it reads a bit like a textbook/infographic poster rather than apparel art, captions are small (~4 mm) for a back print, and there are small garbled marks on the boil-kettle collar.
designs.fix: Add a strong title/headline lockup (e.g. HOW BEER IS MADE at top) and drop or shorten the one-line captions so the steps read as bold illustration rather than a dense diagram; clean the garbled kettle-collar marks.

designs.title: Gin Botanicals
designs.why: Classic vintage botanical-plate look that sells well to gin and cocktail buyers; balanced 2-column layout, elegant italic Latin names, good ink coverage on white. Engraving texture is somewhat wormy/stippled up close (thresholded look) and the orris root plate is the weakest - the leafy fan shape on the right reads as lettuce, not iris.
designs.fix: Add a small title line (e.g. GIN BOTANICALS or 'The Botanicals of Gin') to anchor the plate and tell shoppers what it is at thumbnail size; redraw the orris element as a clear iris rhizome/flower.

designs.title: Vineyard
designs.why: Pleasant Tuscan-style scene, but the rectangle of dense hatching prints as a heavy grey block on the tee, the foreground vines/grapes turn to busy mush at full size, and the generic 'VINEYARD.' label (with an odd full stop) gives no hook or reason to buy at $50 - it reads like stock art.
designs.fix: Open up the image: thin the foreground hatching and fade the edges into a vignette/oval so it breathes on fabric, and replace 'VINEYARD.' with a more specific, ownable title (a region, 'Est.' line or a wine phrase).
